note: PHASE 3, no IMSLP candidates (all 19 composers have imslpWorks 0), so every work is added from publisher tables, Wikipedia lists and commercial recordings. EVIDENCE: Faber Music composer work tables (Adès, Knussen, Anderson, David and Colin Matthews, Benjamin: scoring, year, duration) were opened and parsed; the James Joslin Music chamber worklist for Beamish; Wikipedia lists for the others (Birtwistle, Turnage, MacMillan, Bryars, Nyman, Weir, Grime, Holloway, Ferneyhough). Recordings: Deezer album track lists (album ids in sources) after composer-name album searches (about 450 albums found, about 160 opened, plus about 70 track searches); MusicBrainz was queried but too slow (shared clock) and was dropped. Boosey, Schott, Chester and Wise pages are JavaScript or 403 and were not used; Presto and Naxos Music Library were not used. Apple Music composerTerm searches (19 composers, up to 200 tracks each) were read for chamber titles and added The King's Alchemist (Beamish), Holloway's Horn Quintet Op. 135 and Trio Op. 113 and Turnage's Massarosa. WebSearch: 10 searches (scoring or date of Turnage's This Silence, Maxwell Davies's Ave Maris Stella, Benjamin's Octet, Holloway's Serenade, Grime's Whistler Miniatures, Anderson's Poetry Nearing Silence, Finnis's quartets, Maxwell Davies's Voyage to Fair Isle, Ferneyhough's Fourth Quartet, Frances-Hoad). THE FLOOR was applied strictly: a work is kept only with a commercial recording found; many published works by these composers (Birtwistle's early ensemble pieces, Knussen's Songs without Voices, Turnage's Three Farewells, several quartet cycles by Colin Matthews, Anderson and Grime) were skipped as 'not performed or recorded' only because no recording turned up in the searches, which is weak: they may be recorded on albums that do not carry the composer's name. OWNER MAY RULE: (1) Maxwell Davies's music-theatre pieces (Eight Songs for a Mad King, Miss Donnithorne's Maggot) are skipped as vocal repertoire although recorded with six players and a singer. (2) ASSUMED SCORINGS: Holloway's Serenade in C is entered with the Schubert Octet line-up (clarinet, bassoon, horn, string quintet) because the BIS notes say it follows that model; Turnage's This Silence has its string quintet entered as 2 violins, viola, cello, double bass; Anderson's Poetry Nearing Silence is entered from the NMC recording credits as reported by a search summary; Frances-Hoad's scorings come from a search summary of the composer's site (404 when opened), so her seven entries are 'medium'. (3) Ferneyhough's Fourth Quartet is entered as a string quartet with a soprano (formationNote); David Matthews's Quartet No. 13 has four singers (formation 'other'). (4) Knussen's Ophelia Dances needs a conductor; Turnage's Release has only a double bass as string part. (5) Years are left blank for the Naxos Quartets (only the 2001-07 span and the first performance of No. 1 on 17 Oct 2002 were found), the Little Quartets, Beamish's, Frances-Hoad's older pieces and others where sources disagreed. VIOLIN CATALOGUE: none of the 11 violin entries is cross-listed: 420, 441, 497, 4275 and 4667 are duos (Bryars's Die letzten Tage is for two violins on the recording), 4302 Duet 4 is violin and flute, 4270 The Flittin' violin and clarinet, 4958 Shadow Walker is for two violins and orchestra; 4266 A Book of Seasons, 4440 Shades Lengthen and 4663 Concerto No. 2 are for violin with an ensemble whose size was not confirmed. PROCESS: one accidental `pkill -f NONE` was run once (it matched no process); no other process was stopped except my own by PID. No exclusion proposals: all 19 composers have publisher and recording track records.
